_meta.description: Display information for taxa in the MetaAves Taxon Information Card. Game logic should use taxonomy.json, not this file.

class:Aves.name: Aves
class:Aves.description: Birds are warm-blooded vertebrate animals in the class Aves. They are characterised by feathers, toothless beaks, hard-shelled eggs, high metabolic rates, four-chambered hearts, and lightweight skeletons. Birds occur worldwide and range greatly in size and lifestyle. They evolved from theropod dinosaurs and are the only living dinosaurs.
class:Aves.distributionHabitat: Birds live in ecosystems across the world, from polar regions to tropical forests, deserts, oceans, wetlands, grasslands, and cities.

order:Bucerotiformes.name: Bucerotiformes
order:Bucerotiformes.description: Bucerotiformes is an order of birds that includes hornbills and several closely related groups. Its members are generally characterised by distinctive bills and varied adaptations to life in forests and other habitats.
keyCharacteristics: Includes hornbills and related bird groups
Contains both terrestrial and arboreal forms
order:Bucerotiformes.distributionHabitat: Members occur mainly across Africa and Asia, with different groups occupying forests, woodland, savanna, and other habitats.

family:Bucerotidae.name: Bucerotidae
family:Bucerotidae.description: Hornbills are birds of the family Bucerotidae found mainly in tropical and subtropical Africa, Asia, and Melanesia. They are characterised by long, down-curved bills, often brightly coloured, and many species have a horny casque on the upper mandible. Hornbills are generally omnivorous and commonly nest in natural cavities.
keyCharacteristics: Often nest in natural tree cavities
family:Bucerotidae.distributionHabitat: Hornbills occur mainly in tropical and subtropical forests and woodlands of Africa, Asia, and Melanesia. Many Asian species depend heavily on primary forest.

genus:Buceros.name: Buceros
genus:Buceros.description: Buceros is a genus of large hornbills in the family Bucerotidae. Species in this genus are large-bodied forest hornbills with prominent bills and casques and are strongly associated with mature tropical forests.
keyCharacteristics: Fruit is an important food source
genus:Buceros.distributionHabitat: Species of Buceros occur in tropical South and Southeast Asia, particularly in forested habitats with large mature trees.

genus:Anthracoceros.name: Anthracoceros
genus:Anthracoceros.description: Anthracoceros is a genus of Asian hornbills in the family Bucerotidae. They are generally medium-sized hornbills with contrasting black-and-white plumage and prominent bills, and many species use forests and woodland habitats.
keyCharacteristics: Fruit and small animals in the diet
genus:Anthracoceros.distributionHabitat: Species occur in South and Southeast Asia, using forests, woodland, and other tree-rich habitats.

order:Passeriformes.name: Passeriformes
order:Passeriformes.description: Passeriformes, commonly called passerines or perching birds, is the largest order of birds and includes more than half of all bird species. Passerines generally have an anisodactyl toe arrangement, with three toes pointing forward and one backward, an arrangement well suited to perching.
keyCharacteristics: Includes more than half of bird species
Highly diverse body forms and lifestyles
Many species are insectivorous or omnivorous
order:Passeriformes.distributionHabitat: Passerines occur on every continent except Antarctica and occupy habitats ranging from forests and grasslands to deserts, wetlands, mountains, and urban environments.

family:Passeridae.name: Passeridae
family:Passeridae.description: Passeridae is a family of passerine birds that includes the true sparrows and several closely related groups. Members are generally small to medium-sized birds with stout conical bills adapted for eating seeds and other foods.
keyCharacteristics: Often associated with open or human-modified habitats
family:Passeridae.distributionHabitat: Passerids are distributed mainly across Europe, Africa, and Asia, with several species adapted to agricultural areas, settlements, and other open habitats.

genus:Passer.name: Passer
genus:Passer.description: Passer is a genus of sparrows in the family Passeridae. These birds are generally small, stout-bodied passerines with short tails and strong conical bills, and several species have adapted successfully to human settlements.
keyCharacteristics: Primarily seed-eating, with other foods also taken
genus:Passer.distributionHabitat: Passer species occur across much of Europe, Africa, and Asia, occupying open country, farmland, villages, towns, and cities.
